class.name: NNHTNSearchSettings
class.brief_description: Policy and budgets for an [NNHTNRoot]'s planning.
class.description: Assign to [member NNHTNRoot.search_settings]. Without it the root uses these defaults. One expansion is counted for each method alternative whose conditions are checked, for each primitive task occurrence attempted, and for each collection of an [NNHTNBinding]'s values. Entering compounds, following calls and choosing among [constant NNHTNMethod.PARTIAL_ORDER] orders is free. When a budget runs out the search stops with [constant NNHTNRoot.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED]; see [method NNHTNRoot.get_last_cutoff_reason]. The history settings apply only while [member NNHTNRoot.track_search] is [code]true[/code]; see [method NNHTNRoot.get_search_history]. Invalid values are not clamped: they are listed by [method get_validation_errors], shown as configuration warnings on the root, and make the root do nothing until fixed.

method.name: get_validation_errors
method.description: Returns one message per invalid value. Empty when the settings are valid.

members.member: The most argument candidates used from one [method NNHTNMethod.on_resolve_arguments] call, and the most values used from one collection of an [NNHTNBinding]. Must be at least 1. Leaving candidates or values out makes the search incomplete and sets [method NNHTNRoot.get_last_cutoff_reason]: when no plan is found, the search reports [constant NNHTNRoot.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED] instead of [constant NNHTNRoot.NO_PLAN], and under [constant LOWEST_COST] a plan found is reported with [constant NNHTNRoot.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED] and is not optimal.
The most expansions one search may use. Must be at least 1. For a fixed domain and state, a search bounded only by expansions is deterministic.
The most search attempts [method NNHTNRoot.get_search_history] keeps. Must be at least 1. The oldest attempts are dropped first.

The most bytes of search history kept, measured as the [method @GlobalScope.var_to_bytes] size of each attempt. Must be at least 1024. The oldest attempts are dropped first, but the newest is always kept: its events stop once they and its initial state would exceed half of this limit, its initial state is dropped beyond a quarter, and its plan entries stop beyond a quarter, each marking the attempt [code]truncated[/code].
The most wall-clock time one search may take, in milliseconds. [code]0[/code] means no limit. Must not be negative.

The most decision events recorded for one search attempt. Must be at least 1. Later events are dropped and the attempt is marked [code]truncated[/code]; a truncated trace is not a complete account of the search.
How alternatives are ordered and which plan wins.

constants.constant: Tries methods in scene order and returns the first complete plan. Ignores [member NNHTNMethod.priority] and [member NNHTNTask.estimated_cost].

Tries methods by descending [member NNHTNMethod.priority] or [method NNHTNMethod.on_get_priority], keeping scene order between equal priorities, and returns the first complete plan. Priority is a preference, not a cost; costs are neither read nor validated.

Orders methods like [constant RANKED], then keeps searching after each complete plan and returns the one with the lowest total cost: the sum of every step's [member NNHTNPlanStep.cost], from [member NNHTNTask.estimated_cost] or [method NNHTNTask.on_get_estimated_cost]. Of plans with equal cost, the first found wins. Because costs are non-negative, any partial plan that already costs at least as much as the best plan is abandoned (branch and bound). An invalid cost rejects its occurrence with an error. The result is [code]optimal[/code] only when the whole search space was explored. When a budget or the candidate cap cuts the search short, the cheapest plan found so far is still returned and installed, with [constant NNHTNRoot.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED] and [code]optimal[/code] [code]false[/code].
